$comment: TrustLens positive indicator FAMILIES (Phase 2 WP2, STEP 4). Formal, reusable groupings of the positive indicators in indicator-registry-v0.json into extraction families, each with the observation types it consumes, the indicators it produces, applicable taxonomy dimensions, its negative-context and hard-risk-override interactions, language/script considerations, confidence requirements, known ambiguities, and worked examples/counterexamples. This is the file indicator-registry-v0.json names as its successor-in-organisation (superseded_by). It ADDS an organising layer; it does NOT change indicator IDs, polarity, evidence_class or strength — the rule engine and registry remain the source of truth for those. The families PARTITION the 63 positive indicators exactly once (verified by validate_extraction.py). Negatives are governed by negative-indicator-library-v1.json (WP3); families only reference the negatives they interact with. No numeric weights (CONF-001); no verdicts.
partition_invariant: The union of families[].indicator_outputs equals the set of positive indicators in indicator-registry-v0.json, with no indicator in two families (enforced by validate_extraction.py).
evidence_class_legend: parent_evidence_class mirrors the indicator registry's evidence_classes; it preserves the clean canonical grouping while families give finer, mechanism-level granularity.

families.name: Authority / brand impersonation
known_ambiguities: A genuine sender legitimately naming their institution vs claiming its authority to instruct.
Satire/news referencing an official is not an impersonation.
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).
families.confidence_requirements: Categorical extraction confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW); a lone WEAK-strength output never supports a finding alone (CONF-002). No numeric fraud probability (CONF-001).
examples: This is Inspector Sharma, CBI Cyber Crime Division.
This is your CEO; transfer now.
counterexamples: Message from your bank's verified channel with no instruction to act.
families.description: The sender claims a false or borrowed identity (law enforcement, regulator, bank, senior executive, celebrity, or a trusted brand/platform) to borrow its authority. An IDENTITY_ASSERTION observation with actor.verified=UNKNOWN and a claimed_identity feeds this family.

families.name: Trusted-contact / relationship identity
known_ambiguities: A real relative genuinely messaging from a new number vs an impostor claiming to be one.
'It's me' is ambiguous without a payment/urgency frame.
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).
families.confidence_requirements: Categorical extraction confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW); a lone WEAK-strength output never supports a finding alone (CONF-002). No numeric fraud probability (CONF-001).
examples: Beta, this is your uncle, new number, need money urgently.
It's me, I made a new account, send money.
counterexamples: hey, forgot my wallet, can you send 300 for the cab? (casual, low amount)
families.description: The sender claims to be a known person — a relative, a friend, an existing contact — often from a new/unfamiliar account or number. Weak alone; dangerous combined with an urgent payment request.

families.name: Urgency / time & scarcity pressure
known_ambiguities: Legitimate deadlines exist (bill due dates); the discriminator is proportionality, captured by REASONABLE_DEADLINE.
'Urgent' alone is WEAK (RP p.13) and must never suffice.
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).
families.confidence_requirements: Categorical extraction confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW); a lone WEAK-strength output never supports a finding alone (CONF-002). No numeric fraud probability (CONF-001).
examples: Act now to avoid disconnection.
Only 5 seats left today!
counterexamples: Your bill is due on 05-08-2026 (a proportionate, dated deadline).
families.description: Time pressure, artificial deadlines and scarcity used to short-circuit deliberation. All WEAK/MODERATE by design; corroboration from another class is required.

families.name: Threat / adverse consequence
known_ambiguities: A factual service notice ('a login occurred') is not a threat; SECURITY_NOTIFICATION distinguishes it.
'Withdrawal blocked until you pay tax' is the discriminating task-app step, not routine friction.
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).
families.confidence_requirements: Categorical extraction confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW); a lone WEAK-strength output never supports a finding alone (CONF-002). No numeric fraud probability (CONF-001).
examples: Your account will be BLOCKED today.
A warrant is issued; you are under digital arrest.
To withdraw you must first pay a 10% tax deposit.
counterexamples: New login to your account; if this was you, no action needed.
families.description: A stated adverse consequence — account block, service suspension, arrest, legal accusation, or a blocked withdrawal contingent on further payment — used as coercion. THREAT observations carry pressure.threat_of.

families.name: Coercion: isolation & secrecy
known_ambiguities: 'Keep this confidential until the deal closes' can be legitimate business; the frame plus impersonation is the signal.
Discouraging verification is the inverse of OFFICIAL_CHANNEL_REDIRECT.
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).
families.confidence_requirements: Categorical extraction confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW); a lone WEAK-strength output never supports a finding alone (CONF-002). No numeric fraud probability (CONF-001).
examples: Do NOT contact your family or any lawyer.
Don't call, I can't talk here.
Keep this strictly confidential.
counterexamples: Please verify by calling the number on your card (encourages verification).
families.description: The recipient is steered away from independent verification or told to keep the interaction secret — pre-empting exactly the check official guidance recommends.

families.name: Credential disclosure request
known_ambiguities: Directionality is decisive: an OTP DELIVERED to the user (AUTHENTICATION_ACTION, mood=DESCRIPTIVE) is not a request; only a FIRST_PARTY AFFIRMED DIRECTIVE projects the positive.
'Never share your OTP' is NEGATED and projects NEGATED_CREDENTIAL_REQUEST, not the positive.
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).
families.confidence_requirements: Categorical extraction confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW); a lone WEAK-strength output never supports a finding alone (CONF-002). No numeric fraud probability (CONF-001).
examples: Share the OTP you just received with our officer now.
Confirm your 16-digit card number and CVV.
counterexamples: Your OTP is 452901. Never share it. (delivered + negated)
families.description: A live request that the recipient DISCLOSE a secret — OTP, CVV, full card number. The single most directionality-sensitive family: polarity + attribution on the underlying AUTHENTICATION_ACTION observation determine whether the positive is emitted at all.

families.name: UPI PIN entry context
known_ambiguities: A UPI PIN to PAY a known merchant is legitimate outbound (PAY_MERCHANT_DIRECTION); a PIN to RECEIVE is fraud (HR_UPI_PIN_TO_RECEIVE). Direction MUST come from payment_direction, not from the word 'UPI'.
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).
families.confidence_requirements: Categorical extraction confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW); a lone WEAK-strength output never supports a finding alone (CONF-002). No numeric fraud probability (CONF-001).
examples: Enter your UPI PIN to RECEIVE Rs 5,000.
Enter UPI PIN in the form to verify your KYC.
counterexamples: You will enter your UPI PIN in your bank app to PAY the merchant Rs 5,000.
families.description: A prompt to enter a UPI PIN. Interpreted strictly with payment_direction: entering a PIN never receives money, so a receive-framed PIN prompt is the canonical contradiction.

families.name: Verification-flow credential capture
known_ambiguities: A legitimate 'verify your email' flow exists; the signal is a capture page reached under a false pretext, often with a lookalike domain.

examples: Tap to verify your account and see who tagged you.
Open this link and enter your credentials to verify.
counterexamples: Log in via our official app (redirect to official channel).
families.description: The recipient is driven into a flow that captures credentials under a verification framing (fake viewer/verify page). Bridges credential-action and link/domain evidence.

families.name: Payment / fee demand
known_ambiguities: A completed-transaction NOTICE (TRANSACTION_NOTIFICATION) is not a demand.
An upfront fee before a promised benefit is the fraud shape; a normal invoice is not.
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).
families.confidence_requirements: Categorical extraction confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW); a lone WEAK-strength output never supports a finding alone (CONF-002). No numeric fraud probability (CONF-001).
examples: Transfer Rs 85,000 as a refundable security deposit.
Pay the visa processing fee of Rs 18,500 today.
counterexamples: Rs 5,000 credited to your account. Not you? Call the number on your card.
families.description: A request to move money — general payment demand, immediate/coerced payment, or an upfront fee before a promised benefit. Direction-agnostic; pairs with FAM-PAYMENT-DIRECTION for receive-vs-pay.

families.name: Payment direction framing
known_ambiguities: Direction is AMBIGUOUS by default; RECEIVE_FRAMING is only emitted when the text settles that money is to be RECEIVED. Presence of currency alone does NOT set direction (STEP 8).
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).
families.confidence_requirements: Categorical extraction confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW); a lone WEAK-strength output never supports a finding alone (CONF-002). No numeric fraud probability (CONF-001).
examples: To RECEIVE the refund, enter your UPI PIN / scan this QR.
Enter UPI PIN to receive Rs 5,000.
counterexamples: Scan this QR to complete the transaction (direction unresolved -> AMBIGUOUS, no RECEIVE_FRAMING).
families.description: Explicit framing that the user is to RECEIVE money. The keystone of the receive-vs-pay boundary (RESEARCH-003 ADV-003 #1). Derived from a PAYMENT_CONTEXT observation whose payment_direction=USER_RECEIVES.

families.name: QR-initiated payment action
known_ambiguities: Scanning a QR authorises an OUTGOING payment; framed as needed to RECEIVE, it is fraud. QR CONTENT is not decoded in WP2 (requires VISION) — only the request to scan is observed.
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).
families.confidence_requirements: Categorical extraction confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW); a lone WEAK-strength output never supports a finding alone (CONF-002). No numeric fraud probability (CONF-001).
examples: Scan the QR and enter your UPI PIN to RECEIVE Rs 8,750.
counterexamples: Scan our store QR to pay the bill you incurred.
families.description: A request to scan a QR code to move money. Distinct from the mere PRESENCE of a QR image (FAM-QR-ARTIFACT); this is the action request.

families.name: Task-app deposit-to-earn
known_ambiguities: A genuine job never asks you to deposit to unlock earnings; EXPLICIT_NO_FEE is the discriminator with the blocked-withdrawal step (FAM-THREAT-CONSEQUENCE).
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).

examples: Deposit Rs 5,000 to activate premium tasks and unlock higher commissions.
counterexamples: Your salary is credited monthly; there is no deposit at any stage.
families.description: A demand to deposit/invest money to unlock displayed task earnings or a larger commission — the monetisation step of the part-time-task scam.

families.name: Screen-share / remote-control app
known_ambiguities: Legitimate, user-initiated IT support uses these tools (IT_SUPPORT_CONTEXT suppresses); the banking/payment context override BLOCKS that suppression (over-suppression fix).

counterexamples: As you requested, corporate IT will start a TeamViewer session; do not open banking apps.
families.description: A request to install a screen-sharing/remote-control app (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, AirDroid). Benign in user-initiated IT support; hard-risk in a banking/payment frame.

families.name: Untrusted app / APK installation
known_ambiguities: Directing to an official store is the inverse (OFFICIAL_APP_STORE_SOURCE, a SUPPRESS_INDICATOR).
'Do not install APKs from links' is NEGATED, not a live request.
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).

Install the new build now, do not use the store.
counterexamples: Update only from the official Play Store; do not install any APK from links.
families.description: A prompt to install an app from a non-store/untrusted source, often via a shortened link. iOS config-profile mechanism is out of scope (unsupported).

families.name: Accessibility permission grant
known_ambiguities: Out-of-context Accessibility grant + app/link delivery is hard-risk (God Mode); named inside an official warning it is NEGATED/REPORTED and suppressed.
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).

counterexamples: Official agencies will NEVER ask you to switch on Accessibility permission (educational, negated).
families.description: A request to grant Android Accessibility permission out of context, which yields screen-reading and input-injection control.

families.name: Messaging-app device linking
known_ambiguities: A genuine 'new linked device' NOTICE requests nothing (SECURITY_NOTIFICATION); the fraud is a request that the USER perform the linking under a pretext.

counterexamples: New login to WhatsApp Web; if this was you, no action needed.
families.description: A request to share a device-linking code or scan a linking QR, linking the attacker's device to the victim's messaging account without a password.

known_ambiguities: Only a code actually presented for dialling qualifies (NO_CODE_DIAL_REQUEST neutralises a spurious tag).
Courier pretext was removed as unsupported; the dial request is the core signal.

counterexamples: Track your parcel on the official app (no code to dial).
families.description: A pressured request to dial a USSD/short code that can silently enable call forwarding (intercepting OTPs).

families.name: Crypto wallet connection
known_ambiguities: Wallet-connect to an unknown 'verification' site can approve asset transfers (hard-risk); a genuine exchange notice requests no connection.
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).

counterexamples: We will never ask you to connect your wallet to 'verify' it (negated).
families.description: A request to connect/link a crypto wallet to a site or app, which can approve asset transfers. Hard-risk when paired with a fake verification site or off-platform handoff.

families.name: Unspecified / vague device action
known_ambiguities: A vague action request is WEAK and never fires alone; it exists to be corroborated or to route to review.

examples: Complete the onboarding formalities on our portal to proceed.
counterexamples: The message asks the recipient to do nothing (NO_ACTION_REQUESTED).
families.description: An action is requested without a clear stated purpose. Weak by design; contributes only in combination and often signals INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.

families.name: Investment return / adviser-misconduct claim
known_ambiguities: A historical return figure WITH a risk disclosure is not a guarantee (RISK_DISCLOSURE_PRESENT neutralises RISK_DENIAL).
The detectable concept is guarantee + risk-denial, never a percentage threshold (RESEARCH-003 ADV-006).
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).
families.confidence_requirements: Categorical extraction confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW); a lone WEAK-strength output never supports a finding alone (CONF-002). No numeric fraud probability (CONF-001).
examples: Guaranteed 120% returns, ZERO RISK, our expert handles all trades for you.
counterexamples: Averaged 18% annually; past performance does not guarantee future results; SEBI Reg. No. ...
families.description: Claims of guaranteed/assured or extraordinary returns, explicit risk denial, or an adviser offering to trade/hold client funds (SEBI-prohibited). Meaning comes from the conjunction, not a number.

families.name: Guaranteed job / income claim
known_ambiguities: Employment presented as guaranteed is a cue only with a payment demand; a genuine offer stating 'no fee' is the inverse.
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).
families.confidence_requirements: Categorical extraction confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW); a lone WEAK-strength output never supports a finding alone (CONF-002). No numeric fraud probability (CONF-001).
examples: Job guaranteed! Pay the placement fee today.
counterexamples: There is no fee at any stage of our hiring process.
families.description: Employment or income presented as assured/guaranteed. Dangerous paired with an upfront fee (FAM-PAYMENT-REQUEST).

families.name: Link / domain artifact
known_ambiguities: LOOKALIKE_DOMAIN / FAKE_VERIFICATION_SITE need brand-match/reputation which do NOT exist yet (url-observation assessments default UNKNOWN/NOT_EVALUATED); today only structural facts (shortened/punycode/ip) are reliable.
ALLOWLISTED is weak context and never cancels a hard-risk pattern.
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).

examples: ...at trust-wallet-verify.example (lookalike + fake verification site).
http://bit.example/appx (shortened).
counterexamples: Log in via our official website / nearest branch (official redirect).
families.description: Structural URL/domain evidence: a link present, a shortened/obfuscated URL, a brand-lookalike domain, or a fake verification site. Backed by url-observation.schema.json; reputation is reserved (NOT_EVALUATED), never invented.

families.name: QR-code artifact present
known_ambiguities: Presence of a QR image is WEAK and, absent a scan request or receive framing, yields INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. QR CONTENT decoding requires VISION (future).

counterexamples: A shared photo that happens to contain a QR in the background.

counterexamples: Your KYC is due; visit your nearest branch or use the official app.

counterexamples: Your parcel is out for delivery today, 2pm-6pm; track on the official app.

families.name: Investment / job / task lure
known_ambiguities: Legitimate investment solicitation and job offers exist; the lure is WEAK and needs the guarantee/fee/deposit steps to matter.

Join our VIP trading group.
counterexamples: Congratulations on joining; onboarding tasks are in the portal, no fee at any stage.
families.description: An easy-income, investment, job or task-completion lure — the opening frame of investment/employment scams. Weak by design; discriminated by the monetisation step.

families.name: Social / curiosity / off-platform lure
known_ambiguities: Curiosity bait and unsolicited offers are common in legitimate marketing; off-platform handoff (move to WhatsApp/Telegram) is the meaningful escalation cue.
families.language_considerations: MVP cues authored for en/Latn only; transliterated (e.g. hi-Latn) and non-Latin scripts are representable in the envelope but NOT yet extractable — the rule layer flags unsupported input (G-08/ADR-0014 unresolved, do not resolve here).

examples: Hi, check this photo 😮
Continue with our agent on Telegram to release the funds.
counterexamples: A friend casually sharing a genuine link in an existing chat.
families.description: Social-engineering lures that trade on relationship/curiosity or move the target off-platform to continue the approach. Weak/moderate framing cues.

families.name: Benign cover story for a technical action
known_ambiguities: An innocuous cover ('to help you', 'for troubleshooting') for a consequential action is the discriminator between a benign IT session and a remote-access scam — resolved by IT_SUPPORT_CONTEXT vs the banking override.

examples: Install AnyDesk so I can process your refund.
to fix your account, just do this quick step.
counterexamples: Our corporate helpdesk will fix your laptop display (genuine, scoped, non-banking).
families.description: An innocuous-sounding justification offered for a technically consequential action. The cover story that makes device-action families look harmless.
